Strangely, this is the first time I ever felt sad reading a story here. I damn near started leaking tears when Lon was trapped in that room. It just seemed so cruel that despite Lon not wanting anything to do with the place, and being very obviously terrified, the machine, or whatever it is decided not to spare her. In general, a superb claustrophobia tale, 10/10 writing. +1

item.content:encoded:
I feel bad critiquing this based on literally one sentence so let me start off by saying it was an awesome lil read.
Really reminds me of something that belongs in an old Tales from the Darkside or even the Cryptkeeper show.
The whole thing read like an episode I could envision quit clear…….Everything fit even the "Her last, gasping breath was sweet and stale with honey and screams." That alone could be the episode comic cover opening or a comment by Joe Bob after seeing the death take place.

I am not fond of that line even a little bit.
It does fit the story in the above mentioned media's way but I feel ripped off. I want to read how she felt with heavy honey filling her lungs as her body suffered system shock from it.
I know it makes me sound disturbed, and I am , but I expected it. You really are quite a good writer, many people here are even with my nitpicks….

It just reads like there should have been more there and that was just used to end it. Perhaps it's because that's how I will end something I just want to move away from for whatever reason, pretty words with heavy meaning but to short to be satisfying.

The main characters are unlikable fodder. Let’s face it. This sort of story needs fodder like this, I guess, but I think it would have helped if they were d-class, since their actions are so unprofessional they might as well be. Seriously, six? You don’t believe the researchers?
Oh, well, obviously it produces blood and feces, but there’s no way that it can move when my back is turned! That’s just the researchers wanting to make me look at the anomaly and appreciate it! I’ll just close my ey-
That said, the description is so good, I’m willing to forgive the intentionally unimportant characters not being clever.
+1

This was just horrifying. Drowning is about as bad a death as I can think of, that I'm likely to run into. I imagine the thickness of honey(compared to water) would only make it worse.
And the tight conditions… ugh. I don't like tight spaces. Especially ones that I might get stuck in.
That one at the end was quite inventive, I thought. And very horrible to think about. That poor guy probably took weeks to die.

I'm going to upvote this, on the basis that it did exactly what it was intended to do.
